features.feature_name: and t3a
features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS now support creating clusters using the listed AWS EC2 instance families.

features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS now support creating clusters using the listed AWS EC2 instance families.
features.extended_definition: For Anthos clusters on AWS (previous-generation), the c5a feature means the AWS EC2 c5a instance family is included in the set of supported node instance types for GKE on AWS clusters. features.evidence_summary: The cited page is an official GKE on AWS reference table that enumerates EC2 instance families and versions, and it explicitly includes c5a instance types with supported versions.

features.feature_name: i3en
features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS now support creating clusters using the listed AWS EC2 instance families.
features.extended_definition: Anthos clusters on AWS list the AWS EC2 i3en family as supported node instance types for GKE on AWS, meaning these shapes are eligible when creating clusters/node pools. The documented i3en models include i3en.2xlarge, i3en.3xlarge, i3en.6xlarge, i3en.12xlarge, i3en.24xlarge, i3en.large, i3en.xlarge, and i3en.metal, with minimum supported version values shown in the same matrix.
features.evidence_summary: The referenced official GKE on AWS page provides a supported-instance-type matrix that directly includes i3en instance models and their associated minimum supported cluster/node-pool version values.

features.feature_name: m5ad
features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS now support creating clusters using the listed AWS EC2 instance families.
features.extended_definition: On Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) for AWS, the m5ad feature is support for creating Anthos clusters/node pools using the EC2 M5ad instance family, with specific models listed as m5ad.large, m5ad.xlarge, m5ad.2xlarge, m5ad.4xlarge, m5ad.8xlarge, m5ad.12xlarge, m5ad.16xlarge, and m5ad.24xlarge. The page documents these M5ad models as supported with X86 64-bit architecture and a minimum supported cluster version and node pool version of 1.21.
features.evidence_summary: The referenced Google Cloud documentation is an official support matrix that explicitly lists m5ad instance types and their supported versions for GKE on AWS.

features.feature_name: r5ad
features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS now support creating clusters using the listed AWS EC2 instance families.
features.extended_definition: In Anthos clusters on AWS (GKE on AWS), the `r5ad` feature is the support for AWS EC2 R5ad family instance types in node pools, such as `r5ad.large`, `r5ad.xlarge`, and larger sizes (`r5ad.2xlarge` through `r5ad.24xlarge`). The documentation lists these as supported instance types with x86 64-bit architecture and a minimum supported cluster version of 1.21 and minimum supported node pool version of 1.21.
features.evidence_summary: The cited Google Cloud docs page contains the official supported EC2 instance-type matrix for GKE on AWS, including explicit entries for every R5ad node-pool instance size and their minimum supported versions.

features.feature_name: CMK encryption for component volumes
features.feature_summary: Anthos clusters on AWS supports encrypting component volumes with customer-managed keys (CMK).
features.extended_definition: Anthos clusters on AWS (GKE on AWS) allow operators to enable customer-managed key encryption for key component data stores and volumes by supplying AWS KMS key ARNs in cluster and node-pool creation parameters (for example, `--database-encryption-kms-key-arn` and `--config-encryption-kms-key-arn`). The documentation also specifies separate KMS key ARNs for control plane configuration, etcd/secret data, and control-plane main volume encryption, with required IAM permissions (`kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, and related grant actions), confirming CMK-backed encryption of cluster component volumes and sensitive control-plane artifacts.
features.evidence_summary: The cited GKE on AWS quickstart, cluster-creation, and IAM-role pages collectively document CMK/KMS ARN usage for cluster and node-pool encryption and the exact KMS IAM permissions required for controlling access to encrypted component data and volumes.
